name: Question 8
problem:
Let ${J}_{n}(\lambda )$ denote an $n\times n$ Jordan block with $\lambda $ on the main diagonal. Fill in the missing entries in the matrix below.

|  |  | {{field-1}} | $-3$ | $0$ | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3{J}_{4}(\frac{\pi }{6}))=\,\,$ |  | $0$ | $0$ | {{field-3}} | $0$ |  |
|  | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $-3$ |  |  |

worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and a Jordan block ${J}_{n}(\lambda ),$ we have

$$
f({J}_{n}(\lambda ))=[\begin{aligned}f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & \frac{{f}^{″}(\lambda )}{2!} & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-1)}(\lambda )}{(n-1)!} \\ 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-2)}(\lambda )}{(n-2)!} \\ ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ 0 & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) \\ 0 & ⋯ & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda )\end{aligned}].
$$

In this case, we have $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡3x,$ $n=4,$ and $\lambda =\frac{\pi }{6}.$

Since $n=4,$ we need to compute the first $4-1=3$ derivatives of $f:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-9\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =27\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{4}(\frac{\pi }{6})) & =[\begin{aligned}f(\frac{\pi }{6}) & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & \frac{1}{2!}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & \frac{1}{3!}{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\ 0 & f(\frac{\pi }{6}) & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & \frac{1}{2!}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\ 0 & 0 & f(\frac{\pi }{6}) & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & f(\frac{\pi }{6})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) & -\frac{9}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) & \frac{9}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\text{ } \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) & -\frac{9}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\ 0 & 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 0 & \frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
